title: 2016 AMC 10B Problem 6
statement: Laura added two three-digit positive integers. All six digits in these numbers are different. Laura’s sum is a three-digit number \(S.\) What is the smallest possible value for the sum of the digits of \(S?\)

solutions.text:
To minimize the sum of the addends, use the two smallest nonzero hundreds digits, \(1\) and \(2\), and then the four smallest remaining digits, \(0,3,4,5\). Placing the smaller digits in the tens places shows that every possible sum is at least \(104+235=339\). On the other hand, any three-digit number with digit sum less than \(4\) is at most \(300\). Therefore the digit sum of \(S\) is at least \(4\).

The example \(157+243=400\) uses six distinct digits and has digit sum \(4\). Thus the smallest possible digit sum is \(4\).

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Show a digit sum below \(4\) is impossible
